newsitem.title: KENYA: Drought will hit Kenyan tea until June -report.
newsitem.headline: Drought will hit Kenyan tea until June -report.

text.p: Prolonged dry weather in Kenya's main tea- producing areas has led to a decline in production that is likely to persist until June, a private report said on Wednesday.
The report from Mombasa-based African Tea Broker Ltd. said recovery would be slow even though long-awaited rains had now arrived.

All producing areas had been affected by drought, with the crop put under severe stress. Plucking was much reduced and leaf intake in some areas the lowest on record -- forcing many factories to close.
The report gave a crop figure for February this year of 13.52 million kg, a fall of 39.06 per cent compared with the same month in 1996.
Average prices at Mombasa weekly auctions were $1.78 in February against $1.38 a year earlier.
